messages:
andrea-ng: Heads up — west3 spot GPU pool preflight failed during capacity validation, blocking the handoff to ops-oncall. Putting the failure dump below. :frowning:

sam: OK, what's the error? is it quota or image/driver issues? :eyes:

andrea-ng: Looks quota-ish. infra-bot returned the capacity check fail. Copying the relevant lines:

infra-bot: preflight-check v1.4.2 | region=west3 | pool=spot-gpu-west3
infra-bot: STEP capacity_check => FAILED
infra-bot: reason=INSUFFICIENT_CAPACITY; shortfall=12 gpus; azs_checked=[west3-a,west3-b]; fallback_possible=false
infra-bot: network_check => OK
infra-bot: eni_check => WARN: eni limit close to quota (used 480 / limit 500)

kevin-l: ENI limit is the key here. We're hitting provider-enforced ENI limits in both AZs. Usually shows up when we create lots of small instances (g4dn.*) for spot pools.

maya: Can we switch to fewer larger instances to reduce ENI usage? e.g., use p3dn.24xlarge or similar so ENIs per GPU drop. That'll reduce shortfall without waiting for quota increase.

sam: Agreed as a quick mitigation. Two options: 1) spin up smaller number of bigger instances (manual override in the tfvars) OR 2) file a quota request (slow) + rerun preflight. Which do we want for the handoff timeline?

andrea-ng: Handoff scheduled in 2 hours. Quota request won't land in time. Suggest we try the instance-type swap for the canary and keep rollout paused until cloud quota confirmed.

kevin-l: I'll prepare a tfvar patch. Quick command I'm going to run (dry-run first):

```
# change instance profile to lower ENI footprint
terraform plan -var-file=west3-spot-pool.tfvars -var 'instance_type=p3.8xlarge' -target=module.spot_pool
```

kevin-l: If plan looks good I'll apply only the spot pool module and watch preflight.

infra-bot: monitoring-link: https://infra.redwood/monitors/west3/eni-utilization (current: 96% of quota in west3-a, 92% in west3-b)

ops-oncall: Pause the automated handoff. I'll annotate the runbook and set a blocker flag. :no_entry_sign:

maya: Also hit another edge: the AMI we usually use has a newer driver that fails on p3 in some zones. Please run a small canary instance with the new AMI first (1 instance) so we don't swap and then discover a driver failure.

andrea-ng: Good call. Plan: 1) kevin apply instance-type swap in tf (p3.8xlarge) for the canary, 2) spin single canary VM with new AMI to validate driver, 3) re-run preflight, 4) if green, resume handoff; ops-oncall will coordinate. If driver fails, rollback tf change and we file quota escalation with cloud support.

sam: I can help run the canary and monitor logs. I'll tail the infra agent: `journalctl -u infra-agent -f` and watch kernel/dkms errors.

ops-oncall: I've paused handoff and created blocker ticket INFRA-4621 with notes. Assigned to kevin and andrea. ETA for decision: 60-90m.

andrea-ng: Thanks all. I'll post updates here. For the record: root cause appears to be ENI quota + spot capacity shortage. Temporary mitigation = instance sizing + canary validation.

kevin-l: Starting dry-run now. Will post plan output in ~10m. :hammer:

infra-bot: Reminder: if switching instance families, check compilation of CUDA kernels in the runtime CI matrix — may need to add p3 to build matrix.

andrea-ng: noted. will open follow-up to eng-runtime if canary passes.

sam: +1.

ops-oncall: Acknowledged. Keeping channel updated.
